project.name: lapacho
project.description: Lapacho is a secure clipboard manager in Rust: a Tauri 2 + Leptos desktop app with encrypted SQLite history, a secret-masking sensitivity classifier and threat scanner, plus an Android keyboard (Kotlin IME) that shares the same core via a uniffi bridge and offers on-device word suggestions and spell correction.

nodes.name: crypto.rs
nodes.summary: AES-256-GCM encryption at rest plus in-memory key handling: a zeroize-on-drop SecretKey and a resident Cipher that the consuming app builds from a key it provisions itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Drop + zeroize so key material is wiped when released; the resident Cipher is the secret worth mlock-ing.

nodes.name: detectors.rs
nodes.summary: Content-type detector that classifies raw clipboard text into a DetectedType (plain text, URL, JSON, SVG, Mermaid, and so on).

nodes.name: ingest.rs
nodes.summary: Ingest pipeline that turns a raw clipboard string into a classified, sanitized and display-masked ClipboardItem by composing detectors, security and types.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root of lapacho-core: declares the ten core modules and re-exports the public API (ingest, spotlighting, threat assessment, storage repo and domain types).
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root using `pub mod` plus `pub use` re-exports to form a flat public surface.

nodes.name: llm.rs
nodes.summary: Prompt-injection defenses for sending clipboard content to an LLM: applies spotlighting with random nonce fences to segregate untrusted data from instructions, plus an image guard prompt.

nodes.name: locked_ring.rs
nodes.summary: Fixed-capacity, page-locked (mlock) ring buffer that holds the session buffer's plaintext in RAM without it being swapped, scrubbing slots on removal and drop.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses unsafe mlock/munlock on a preallocated region and explicit scrubbing in Drop to keep plaintext out of swap.

nodes.name: SecretKey
nodes.summary: Zeroize-on-drop wrapper around raw key bytes with generate, byte/base64 constructors and controlled exposure.

nodes.name: Cipher
nodes.summary: Resident AES-256-GCM cipher built from a SecretKey, providing encrypt/decrypt of payloads.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Builds a Cipher from a SecretKey, initializing the AES-256-GCM state.

nodes.name: encrypt_with
nodes.summary: Encrypts plaintext with a fresh random nonce, prefixing the nonce to the ciphertext.

nodes.name: decrypt_with
nodes.summary: Splits nonce from ciphertext and decrypts it, returning an error on authentication failure.

nodes.name: key_from_base64
nodes.summary: Parses a base64 string into a 32-byte key, validating length.

nodes.name: classify_text
nodes.summary: Heuristically classifies clipboard text into a DetectedType such as URL, JSON, SVG or Mermaid.

nodes.name: safe_credential_hint
nodes.summary: Produces a non-revealing hint (e.g. known secret prefix) for masked credential display.

nodes.name: sensitive_display
nodes.summary: Returns the masked display string for content based on its sensitivity level.

nodes.name: process_text
nodes.summary: Classifies, sanitizes and masks raw clipboard text and wraps it into a new ClipboardItem with UUID and timestamp.

nodes.name: fence_nonce
nodes.summary: Generates a random nonce used to build unforgeable fences around untrusted content.

nodes.name: spotlight_text
nodes.summary: Wraps untrusted clipboard text in nonce fences with a system prompt telling the LLM to treat it as data only.

nodes.name: Spotlight
nodes.summary: Result of spotlighting: the system prompt and the fenced user payload to send to an LLM.

nodes.name: LockedRing
nodes.summary: Page-locked fixed-capacity ring of plaintext slots with store/get/remove/clear and scrubbing on drop.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Allocates the ring region and attempts to mlock it, recording whether locking succeeded.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Writes plaintext into the next slot, evicting and scrubbing the oldest entry when full.

nodes.name: plugins.rs
nodes.summary: Plugin subsystem: initializes the plugins directory, loads plugin definitions from disk and executes external plugin processes with a timeout, sanitizing and classifying their output.

nodes.name: security.rs
nodes.summary: Sensitivity classifier and sanitizers: strips control chars, sanitizes SVG against XSS, and heuristically detects secrets, API-key prefixes, recovery keys, backup codes, emails and phone numbers.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of OnceLock-cached regexes and Shannon entropy to separate random secrets from ordinary text.

nodes.name: storage.rs
nodes.summary: Encrypted SQLite history store: the HistoryRepo trait and its SqliteRepo implementation handling save, search, pin/vault, retention cleanup, forbidden-item purge, compaction and preferences.
nodes.languageNotes: Trait-based repository (HistoryRepo: Send + Sync) with rusqlite behind it, encrypting columns via crate::crypto.

nodes.name: threats.rs
nodes.summary: Modular threat-assessment registry for the save/export path: a Detector trait with a static registry of detectors (active content, trojan-source bidi, zero-width chars, prompt/SQL injection, sensitive data, etc.) that never alters content.
nodes.languageNotes: Zero-sized unit structs implementing a trait, collected in a `static &[&dyn Detector]` registry.

nodes.name: types.rs
nodes.summary: Core domain types shared across the app: Sensitivity levels, DetectedType, PersistLevel policy, ClipboardItem, its UI projection UIClipboardItem, and plugin definition/response structs.
nodes.languageNotes: Derives PartialOrd/Ord on Sensitivity so enum order encodes severity.

nodes.name: sanitize_svg

nodes.name: shannon_entropy

nodes.name: is_plain_public_url

nodes.name: bindings.rs

nodes.languageNotes: Uses #[wasm_bindgen] extern blocks with js_namespace and catch to import async JS functions as Rust futures; window label is looked up via js_sys::Reflect to avoid instantiation failures from missing static imports.

nodes.languageNotes: Structs and enums are duplicated rather than shared because lapacho-core would pull rusqlite's C dependencies into the WASM build.

tour.title: What Lapacho Is
tour.description: Start with the README: Lapacho is a secure clipboard manager for the desktop and Android that classifies, sanitizes and masks content before it ever reaches a UI, releasing the original only when you explicitly paste it back. It introduces the security flow this tour follows (capture, type classification, sensitivity classification, masking, persistence policy, release on paste) and the Android keyboard that reuses the same core.

tour.title: Workspace and Core Crate
tour.description: The Cargo workspace ties together lapacho-core, lapacho-predict, the placeholder lapacho-sync, the Android rust-bridge and the Tauri backend. lapacho-core's lib.rs is the hub of the graph: it declares the ten core modules and re-exports the public API that both apps consume, so every later step is one of its modules or one of its consumers.
tour.languageLesson: In Rust, lib.rs is the crate root: `mod foo;` pulls in a module file and `pub use foo::Bar;` re-exports it, letting a crate present a flat public API while keeping its internals split into files. Cargo features (like the optional `mlock` feature here) compile code in or out per consumer.

tour.title: The Domain Vocabulary
tour.description: types.rs is the most depended-upon file in the project. It defines Sensitivity (None / Personal / Credential / Secret), DetectedType, the PersistLevel policy (Paranoia / Balanced / All), ClipboardItem, and UIClipboardItem, the masked projection that is the only thing a UI ever receives. Keeping raw content and its display form as separate types is the core design decision behind the whole security model.
tour.languageLesson: Rust enums are sum types: a value is exactly one variant, and `match` must handle all of them, so adding a new sensitivity level forces every consumer to be updated at compile time.

tour.title: Capture to Classified Item
tour.description: The ingest pipeline is where a raw clipboard string becomes a ClipboardItem. It first asks detectors.rs what kind of content this is (plain text, URL, JSON, SVG, Mermaid, Markdown), then composes the security and threat modules from the next steps to classify, sanitize and produce the display mask. Read ingest.rs as the table of contents for steps 5 through 7.

tour.title: Sensitivity Classification and Masking
tour.description: security.rs decides how dangerous a clip is: regex patterns for API-key prefixes, private keys, credit cards and emails, combined with Shannon entropy to catch random-looking secrets. It also strips control characters and sanitizes SVG against XSS. The Sensitivity it assigns drives the masking (`••••last4` for secrets, `first3…last4` for credentials) and the persistence policy applied later.

tour.title: Threat Scanner and LLM Defenses
tour.description: threats.rs is a registry of Detector implementations run on the save and export path (active content, trojan-source bidi characters, injection patterns), while llm.rs fences untrusted clipboard text with random-nonce spotlighting before it is sent to a model. The test-payloads folder holds the malicious Markdown, Mermaid and plain-text samples used to check these defenses by hand.
tour.languageLesson: A trait plus a static list of trait objects (`&[&dyn Detector]`) is Rust's lightweight plugin registry: adding a detector means implementing the trait and appending it, with no dynamic loading.

tour.title: Secrets in Memory and at Rest
tour.description: crypto.rs provides AES-256-GCM encryption and a SecretKey that zeroizes itself on drop, and locked_ring.rs keeps the session buffer's plaintext in a fixed-size, mlock'ed ring so it is never swapped to disk and is scrubbed on removal. Together they explain why the raw content from Step 3 can exist in the process without leaking.
tour.languageLesson: The `Drop` trait runs code when a value goes out of scope; crates like `zeroize` use it to overwrite key bytes deterministically, something a garbage-collected language cannot guarantee.

tour.title: Encrypted History and Persistence Policy
tour.description: storage.rs defines the HistoryRepo trait and its SqliteRepo implementation: content is encrypted with the cipher from Step 7 before touching SQLite, and the PersistLevel from Step 3 decides what may be written at all (Paranoia stores only non-sensitive items, Balanced adds TTL for credentials, All stores everything). It also handles search, pin/vault, retention cleanup and forbidden items.

tour.title: Plugins Through the Same Pipeline
tour.description: plugins.rs loads plugin definitions from disk and runs them as external processes with a timeout, then sanitizes their output. The integration test plugin_to_history.rs locks the contract that ties Steps 4 to 8 together: plugin output is ingested, stored raw in the encrypted history, and masked for display like any other clip.

tour.title: Desktop Backend (Tauri)
tour.description: The Tauri backend is the first consumer of lapacho-core. main.rs owns the clipboard monitor (X11 polling and a Wayland watcher), the in-memory SessionBuffer and the SQLite history, and exposes Tauri commands to the UI; keystore.rs provisions the history key from the OS keyring with a 0600 file fallback, and images.rs turns clipboard pixels into safe items. tauri.conf.json declares the hidden main window and the frameless Spotlight window.
tour.languageLesson: A Tauri command is a Rust function annotated with `#[tauri::command]`; the frontend calls it by name through IPC, and only commands listed in the builder and allowed by capability files are reachable.

tour.title: Tray Menu and Its Cost
tour.description: tray.rs builds the native tray menu of recent clips, rebuilt on a debounce when history changes, with click-to-copy and per-item thumbnails. The implementation note explains the change that rebuilds the menu without hitting the database; per the README, this rebuild is still where most end-to-end latency lives.

tour.title: Leptos UI and Release on Paste
tour.description: The desktop frontend is a separate WASM crate that deliberately does not depend on lapacho-core, so rusqlite never enters the browser bundle; types.rs mirrors only the masked UI types, and bindings.rs wraps Tauri invoke/listen in typed async calls. app.rs renders the history list and spotlight.rs the quick-search window; neither ever sees raw content, which the backend releases only when an item is pasted.
tour.languageLesson: Leptos uses fine-grained reactive signals: reading a signal inside a view subscribes that DOM node, so only it updates when the signal changes, with no virtual DOM diff.

tour.title: Android Architecture Plan
tour.description: The Android app is a keyboard, not a background monitor: Android only allows reading the clipboard while an input method has focus, so capture happens there. The architecture document lays out the module layout and reuse of lapacho-core, the migration plan describes replacing the Kotlin storage with the Rust core via uniffi, and the manifest runs the IME in its own `:ime` process with backups disabled.

tour.title: The uniffi Bridge
tour.description: rust-bridge/src/lib.rs exposes lapacho-core and lapacho-predict to Kotlin: the same sensitivity classifier from Step 5, an encrypted SQLite history (MobileCore), and a word predictor. build-android.sh cross-compiles it with cargo-ndk and generates Kotlin bindings, and Classify.kt is the Kotlin side that decides when a clip is secret and must be masked in the strip.
tour.languageLesson: uniffi generates foreign-language bindings from annotated Rust (`#[uniffi::export]`, `#[derive(uniffi::Object)]`): the Rust side compiles to a cdylib loaded via JNA, and Kotlin gets idiomatic classes and exceptions instead of hand-written JNI.

tour.title: The Keyboard and Its Paste Strip
tour.description: LapachoIme.kt is the heart of the Android app: an InputMethodService with a paste strip of history clips, on-device suggestions and corrections, and private-field detection so password and incognito fields are never captured (checked by PrivateFieldTest). HistoryRepo.kt and LapachoCipher.kt store history encrypted with a non-exportable Android Keystore key shared by the IME and the companion app.
tour.languageLesson: Running the IME in a separate process (`android:process=":ime"`) isolates the keyboard's memory from the companion activity; the two share state only through the encrypted database and Keystore key.

tour.title: Word Prediction Engine
tour.description: lapacho-predict is a dependency-light crate (serde only) that loads frequency dictionaries plus learned words, completes words by prefix with accent folding, and proposes spelling corrections. real_typos.rs tests correction against the shipped Spanish and English dictionaries, checking that real typos get fixed and real words are left alone. Predict.kt manages bundled and imported dictionaries on the Kotlin side.

tour.title: Dictionaries and Rejected Designs
tour.description: DICTIONARIES.md explains the plain-text frequency format, how several imported dictionaries mix, and how to build your own; DECISIONS.md records approaches evaluated and rejected, such as in-keyboard downloads, a language switch key, autocorrect-on-space and learn-while-typing. Those decisions explain what you see in MainActivity.kt: corrections are offered in the strip but never applied automatically, and words are learned only when you add them explicitly.

tour.title: Status and Next Steps
tour.description: To close, ROADMAP.md shows where the project stands and which technologies were deliberately left out, and lapacho-sync is the placeholder for the planned end-to-end encrypted sync between devices. install.sh shows how the desktop app from Steps 10-12 is built and installed with an autostart entry.
